newsitem.title: INDIA: EU asks India to end all import curbs in two years.
newsitem.headline: EU asks India to end all import curbs in two years.

text.p: The European Union on Friday urged India to lift restrictions on imports within two years, saying the South Asian nation's economy was strong enough to face global competition.
"It is the view of the EU that the import restrictions maintained by India should be eliminated within a two-year period," the European Commission said at the end of two days of talks in New Delhi.
The talks followed consultations at the World Trade Organisation (WTO) in Geneva in December 1995 and in January of this year, the commission said in a statement released in the Indian capital.

"The positive developments and the performance in the Indian economy in recent years, as confirmed by the IMF, no longer justify import restrictions for balance of payments purposes," it said, referring to the International Monetary Fund.
India has agreed to present the WTO in June with a time-table to phase out restrictions on imports.
"It is just another move by the EU to keep the pressure on India to open its economy," trade analyst Arun Goyal said.
Goyal told Reuters domestic industry would protest any move by the government to suddenly lift curbs on imports.

India's businessmen have complained of being swamped by multinational companies after India opened up its economy and liberalised trade and industry as part of reforms launched in 1991 by former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao.
"The government would also like to give the domestic industry time to modernise and compete in the global markets," Goyal said.
Indian Commerce Minister Bolla Buli Ramaiah has said he wants to announce a "big, dynamic" trade policy by the end of March.
The government is scheduled to announce a new import-export policy on March 31.
In February the Commerce Ministry liberalised import rules for at least 161 products, including certain consumer goods.

India and the EU will meet in Brussels next month to continue their talks on the phasing out of import restrictions, it said. "Further talks are expected in the run-up to formal consultations to be resumed in June in WTO," the commission statement said.
The European Union is the top investor in India, it added.
"In 1995, the EU accounted for $231.74 million worth of actual investment in India, equivalent to 11.64 percent of total foreign direct investment coming to India."
